programmeContext.note: Public programme highlights corroborate themes. The current structured guide and module records govern exact credit and progression.

identity: Standalone full-time Physics BSc, not the double degree or the individually planned part-time route. The required upper years include English-taught modules alongside Dutch teaching.
ledger: This elective requires forming a team and discussing the project with the lecturer before the course starts.
This elective builds on analysis and statistical physics.
Students can fill this space with a minor, an approved elective programme or a physics course package.
This elective builds on analysis, linear algebra and classical electrodynamics.
grouping: 60 required in year one, 51 required plus 9 restricted in year two, 30 open plus 3 restricted plus 27 required in year three. Module pages independently confirm the distinct 20, 3, 1 and 3 EC research components. The undergraduate research project is normally experimental.
progression: The current full-time standalone Physics ledger has 60 EC in year one, 51 required plus 9 restricted in year two, and 30 open profile, 3 restricted and 27 research-related EC in year three. The example uses Experimental Projects and Fluid Phenomena in Soft Matter in year two and Relativistic Electrodynamics in year three. Experimental Projects requires a team and advance project discussion. Fluid Phenomena recommends analysis and statistical physics. Relativistic Electrodynamics assumes both introductory analysis courses, both linear algebra courses and Classical Electrodynamics. Research normally follows completion of years one and two and requires study-adviser approval. The adviser assesses exceptions for outstanding courses. The standard project runs 17 weeks in a Leiden physics group, primarily in experimental physics. The 27 EC block comprises the 20 EC project, 3 EC thesis, 1 EC presentation and 3 EC research skills and integrity.

interests.interest: understanding the fundamental laws of nature
interests.assessment: The degree systematically develops laws of motion, fields and matter. UCR sustains selected applied physical laws with real measurements, while fundamental physics remains unfilled.

interests.interest: using mathematics to describe physical phenomena
interests.assessment: Mathematical methods recur across the degree. UCR calculus, Fourier methods and dynamic models are strong direct overlap.
Physical experiments and theory are integrated at Leiden. UCR has wave, materials and geophysical work, with different depth and instrumentation.
Quantitative problem solving and computational modelling are directly taught.
Soft materials and statistical physics exemplify matter and energy. UCR covers applied materials, thermodynamics and energy conversion.
The required project is original physics research. UCR’s scheduled Earth and energy projects support related research skills.
Kinematic modelling is a partial bridge, with Newtonian and analytical mechanics remaining deeper at Leiden.
Applied geophysical surveys touch fields. Leiden has a dedicated theoretical sequence.
Dedicated quantum sequence remains a gap.
Thermodynamics is taught in physical contexts. UCR applies basic thermodynamics and energy balances.
Leiden connects microscopic behaviour and macroscopic thermodynamics. UCR mathematical statistics is different.
Wave interference, spectra and Fourier methods support a partial alignment.
Materials measurements do not cover the solid-state physics sequence.
Modern physics supports the topic. No additional particle or nuclear physics option is inferred.
Relativistic electrodynamics is a valid restricted elective, not common to all pathways.
Substantial common mathematical foundations, with different later development.
Python is explicit. UCR teaches general programming and mathematical models across courses.
Measured data analysis is explicit. UCR offers field/lab measurements and statistical tools.
Physical modelling is a programme-level interest independently supported by mathematics and actual physical applications.
Lab practice is cumulative at Leiden; UCR measurement is in environmental and material contexts.
